laws.rule: Under the Odisha Excise Act, 2008 (Odisha Act 10 of 2013), no person may possess an intoxicant that was not obtained from a licensed vendor, with listed exceptions, including an intoxicant lawfully imported or authorised by the Collector, and foreign or India-made foreign liquor bought for bona fide private consumption and not for sale. A person who is not licensed to manufacture, collect or sell may not possess more than the quantity the State Government has declared as the limit, except under a Collector's permit. The Act itself does not state that quantity.

No intoxicant may be imported unless the State Government has permitted it, any conditions are met, and any excise duty has been paid, except an article already imported into India and liable to customs duty. Quantities above a limit notified by the State Government also need a Collector's pass. No intoxicant may be sold except under a licence from the Collector.

A licensed vendor may not sell any intoxicant to a person who is drunk or intoxicated, or sell or deliver any spirit to a person apparently under the age of 21, whether for consumption by that person or another, on or off the premises. The vendor may not permit drunkenness, intoxication, disorderly conduct or gaming on the premises.

A person licensed to sell foreign liquor or India-made foreign liquor for consumption on the premises may not employ anyone under 18, or any woman, in the part of the premises where the public consumes that liquor, unless a permission endorsed on the licence says otherwise for women. A country-spirit licensee may not employ anyone under 18 where that spirit is sold. A District or Sub-Divisional Magistrate may require a shop to close for the preservation of public peace.

items.text: Under the Odisha Excise Act, 2008 (Odisha Act 10 of 2013), a licensed vendor may not sell or deliver spirit to anyone apparently under 21, or sell any intoxicant to a person who is drunk or intoxicated, and may not permit drunkenness or intoxication on the premises. Liquor generally has to have been obtained from a licensed vendor, and amounts above the government-declared possession limit need a Collector's permit; the Act does not itself state that limit.
